legpress.name: Leg press
how: Set the seat so your lower back and hips stay supported.
Place feet about shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Unlock the safety catches as instructed by the machine; lower slowly within a comfortable range.
Press through the whole foot without locking your knees.
mistakes: Letting the lower back round away from the pad.
Allowing knees to collapse inward.
Loading too much weight or snapping knees straight.
legpress.cue: Smooth down, smooth up. Keep your hips against the pad.
legpress.videoLabel: How To: Leg Press · Scott Herman Fitness

alternative.name: Dumbbell goblet squat to a bench
alternative.steps: 1. Hold one light dumbbell close to your chest, or start with no weight. 2. Sit back toward a sturdy bench or chair under control. 3. Stand by pushing through your whole foot. 4. Keep knees tracking in line with toes and use a pain-free depth.

latpulldown.name: Lat pulldown
how: Adjust the thigh pad so you are secure without pinching.
Use a comfortable grip a little wider than shoulder width.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest while keeping your torso steady.
Let the bar rise slowly; keep shoulders controlled.
mistakes: Pulling the bar behind your neck.
Swinging backward to move the weight.
Shrugging or yanking the bar.
latpulldown.cue: Elbows down toward your sides; no swinging.
latpulldown.videoLabel: How To: Lat Pulldown · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Supported one-arm dumbbell row
alternative.steps: 1. Place one hand on a sturdy bench and hinge forward with a flat back. 2. Hold a light dumbbell in the other hand. 3. Pull your elbow toward your hip without twisting your torso. 4. Lower slowly and repeat on both sides.

chestpress.name: Chest press machine
how: Adjust seat so handles line up around mid-chest.
Keep your back against the pad and feet flat.
Press forward smoothly without locking elbows hard.
Return slowly until you feel a comfortable stretch, not pain.
mistakes: Setting handles too far behind the body.
Arching excessively or shrugging shoulders.
Continuing through chest or shoulder pain.
chestpress.cue: Start light. If your chest is still sore, skip this exercise.
chestpress.videoLabel: How To: Dumbbell Bench Press · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Dumbbell floor press
alternative.steps: 1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and dumbbells resting near your hips. 2. Lie back carefully and position the weights beside your chest. 3. Press up smoothly with wrists stacked over elbows. 4. Lower until upper arms gently touch the floor; use very light weights and only after chest soreness resolves.

legcurl.name: Seated leg curl
how: Adjust the machine pivot to align with your knee joint.
Place the lower pad just above your heels and secure the thigh pad.
Curl the pad down smoothly without lifting your hips.
Return slowly; do not let the stack slam.
mistakes: Incorrect knee alignment.
Using momentum or a load you cannot control.
Letting the weight crash back.
legcurl.videoLabel: How To: Seated Leg Curl · BUFF DUDES

alternative.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
alternative.steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and a very light dumbbell in each hand. 2. Keep knees slightly bent and push hips backward. 3. Lower the weights close to your legs while keeping your back neutral. 4. Stand by bringing hips forward; stop the descent before your back rounds. Learn the hip hinge first.

cablerow.name: Seated cable row
how: Sit tall with knees slightly bent and feet braced.
Begin with arms extended but shoulders controlled.
Pull the handle toward your lower ribs without jerking.
Return slowly without rounding your lower back.
mistakes: Rocking the torso to move the weight.
Rounding the back.
Pulling elbows too far behind you.
cablerow.cue: Keep the torso steady; let the back do the work.
cablerow.videoLabel: How To: Seated Cable Row · Jeremy Ethier

alternative.name: One-arm dumbbell row with support
alternative.steps: 1. Place one hand and one knee on a stable bench. 2. Keep your back flat and hold a light dumbbell in the other hand. 3. Pull your elbow toward your hip without twisting your torso. 4. Lower slowly and repeat on both sides.

gobletsquat.name: Goblet squat to bench
how: Start with a chair or bench behind you; begin without a weight if needed.
Stand with feet around shoulder-width apart.
Bend hips and knees to sit toward the bench with control.
Stand by pushing through your feet; keep knees tracking in line with toes.
mistakes: Dropping onto the bench.
Heels lifting or knees collapsing inward.
Choosing a depth that causes pain.
gobletsquat.cue: Use bodyweight until the movement feels stable.
gobletsquat.videoLabel: How To: Goblet Squat · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Chair squat
alternative.steps: 1. Put a sturdy chair against a wall. 2. Stand with feet around shoulder-width apart. 3. Sit back slowly until you touch the seat lightly. 4. Stand up smoothly; use hands for support if needed.

chestrow.name: Chest-supported row
how: Adjust the chest pad and seat so the handles are reachable.
Keep chest comfortably against the pad.
Pull handles toward your torso without shrugging.
Lower slowly to the starting position.
mistakes: Lifting chest off the pad.
Shrugging shoulders.
Using momentum or too much weight.
chestrow.cue: Stay connected to the pad throughout each rep.
chestrow.videoLabel: How To: One-Arm Dumbbell Row · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: One-arm dumbbell row with support
alternative.steps: 1. Support one hand on a sturdy bench. 2. Hinge at the hips with a flat back. 3. Pull the dumbbell toward your hip without rotating. 4. Lower slowly and repeat on the other side.

shoulderpress.name: Shoulder press machine
how: Adjust seat so handles begin around shoulder height.
Keep your back supported and feet planted.
Press upward in a comfortable range without forcing the elbows straight.
Lower slowly and stop if there is shoulder pain.
mistakes: Starting with handles too low behind the shoulders.
Arching the back.
Forcing painful range or using heavy weight.
shoulderpress.cue: Skip if shoulder or arm soreness remains.
shoulderpress.videoLabel: How To: Overhead Press · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
alternative.steps: 1. Sit against a stable upright bench with a light dumbbell in each hand. 2. Start with weights around shoulder height and elbows slightly forward. 3. Press upward only through a comfortable range. 4. Lower slowly; skip this movement if you have shoulder or arm pain.

legextension.name: Leg extension
how: Align the machine pivot with your knee joint.
Position the shin pad just above the ankle.
Straighten knees smoothly without kicking.
Lower under control; use a comfortable range.
mistakes: Incorrect seat setup.
Swinging or kicking the weight.
Ignoring knee pain.
legextension.cue: Control both directions and keep the load light.
legextension.videoLabel: How To: Leg Extension · Scott Herman Fitness

alternative.name: Goblet squat to a bench
alternative.steps: 1. Hold a light dumbbell close to your chest or start without weight. 2. Sit back toward a sturdy bench. 3. Stand smoothly while keeping knees aligned with toes. 4. Use a comfortable range and stop if your knees hurt.

deadbug.name: Dead bug
how: Lie on your back with arms up and hips and knees bent.
Gently brace your abdomen; keep your lower back comfortably steady.
Slowly extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Return and alternate sides without rushing.
mistakes: Arching the lower back.
Moving too quickly.
Holding your breath.
deadbug.cue: Make the movement smaller if you lose control.

alternative.name: Dead bug (bodyweight is the best beginner option)
alternative.steps: 1. Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent at 90 degrees. 2. Gently brace your abdomen. 3. Slowly extend one arm and the opposite leg. 4. Return and switch sides; make the range smaller if your lower back arches.

chairsquat.name: Chair squat
how: Use a sturdy chair placed against a wall.
Stand in front with feet around shoulder-width apart.
Reach hips back and bend knees to touch or lightly sit on the chair.
Stand smoothly without pushing off your thighs if comfortable.
mistakes: Chair sliding away.
Dropping onto the seat.
Knees collapsing inward.
chairsquat.cue: Use your hands for support if needed.
chairsquat.videoLabel: Goblet Squat (scales to chair squat) · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Dumbbell goblet squat to a bench
alternative.steps: 1. Once bodyweight chair squats feel controlled, hold one light dumbbell close to your chest. 2. Sit back toward a sturdy chair. 3. Stand smoothly. 4. Keep the movement pain-free and avoid dropping onto the seat.

wallpushup.name: Wall push-up
how: Stand facing a solid wall, hands a little wider than shoulders.
Step back until it feels easy; keep your body in a straight line.
Bend elbows and bring chest toward the wall.
Push back smoothly. Only do this once chest and arm soreness have resolved.
mistakes: Hands too high or too low.
Hips sagging or head reaching forward.
Continuing despite pain.
wallpushup.cue: Make it easier by standing closer to the wall.
wallpushup.videoLabel: The Perfect Push Up · Jeremy Ethier (6M+ views)

alternative.name: Dumbbell floor press
alternative.steps: 1. Lie on the floor with knees bent and light dumbbells beside your chest. 2. Press up without bouncing or locking elbows hard. 3. Lower until upper arms gently touch the floor. 4. Do not use this while your chest or arms are still sore.

glutebridge.name: Glute bridge
how: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Brace gently and press through your feet.
Lift hips until shoulders, hips, and knees form a comfortable line.
Lower slowly without over-arching your back.
mistakes: Overarching the lower back.
Feet too far away.
Rushing the lowering phase.

alternative.name: Dumbbell glute bridge
alternative.steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. 2. Rest a light dumbbell across your hips and hold it securely with both hands. 3. Squeeze glutes and lift hips without arching your lower back. 4. Lower slowly. Start with bodyweight first.

calfraise.name: Supported calf raise
how: Stand tall and lightly hold a stable support.
Rise onto the balls of your feet.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly with control.
mistakes: Bouncing.
Leaning heavily on the support.
Rushing the lowering phase.
calfraise.cue: Use a small, controlled range at first.
calfraise.videoLabel: How To: Calf Raises (Science-Based) · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Dumbbell calf raise
alternative.steps: 1. Stand tall and hold a light dumbbell in one hand while the other hand holds a stable support. 2. Rise onto the balls of your feet. 3. Pause at the top. 4. Lower slowly; keep balance secure.

hipthrust.name: Barbell hip thrust
how: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a barbell across your hips.
Plant feet flat, about hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your body is level.
Lower slowly; avoid letting your lower back arch excessively.
mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top.
Feet too far or too close to the body.
Not using a pad on the barbell.
hipthrust.cue: Squeeze at the top for a full second before lowering.
hipthrust.videoLabel: How To: Barbell Hip Thrust · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Dumbbell glute bridge
alternative.steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. 2. Place a dumbbell across your hips and hold it securely. 3. Drive hips upward, squeezing glutes at the top. 4. Lower slowly and repeat.

inclinebench.name: Incline dumbbell press
how: Set a bench to 30–45 degrees and sit with a dumbbell on each knee.
Kick the weights up as you lie back, positioning them near your upper chest.
Press upward until your arms are nearly straight, wrists stacked over elbows.
Lower under control until you feel a comfortable stretch.
mistakes: Bench angle too steep (above 60°) — shifts load away from chest.
Flaring elbows too wide — strains shoulder joints.
Bouncing the weights off the chest.
inclinebench.cue: Think 'press up and slightly back' to target the upper chest.
inclinebench.videoLabel: How To: Incline Dumbbell Press · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Incline push-up
alternative.steps: 1. Place your hands on an elevated surface (bench, box) a little wider than shoulder-width. 2. Keep a straight line from head to heels. 3. Lower your chest toward the surface. 4. Push back up smoothly.

cablefly.name: Cable chest fly
how: Set both cable pulleys to chest height and attach single-handle attachments.
Step forward one foot, holding one handle in each hand with arms open.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Return slowly with control; do not let the weight pull you back aggressively.
mistakes: Bending elbows too much — turns it into a press.
Using too heavy a load and losing range of motion.
Shrugging the shoulders up.
cablefly.cue: Imagine hugging a big tree — round arms, not locked elbows.
cablefly.videoLabel: How To: Cable Chest Fly · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Dumbbell fly on floor
alternative.steps: 1. Lie on the floor with knees bent and a dumbbell in each hand. 2. Start with arms out to the side, elbows soft. 3. Bring the weights together above your chest in a wide arc. 4. Lower slowly until upper arms touch the floor.

facepull.name: Cable face pull
how: Set the cable pulley to eye height and attach a rope.
Hold the rope with both hands, palms facing in, and step back.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends and driving elbows out and back.
Return slowly with controlled tension.
mistakes: Pulling too low — becomes a row, not a face pull.
Using too heavy a load and losing form.
Not externally rotating the shoulders at the end.
facepull.cue: Drive elbows back and apart — think 'double biceps pose'.
facepull.videoLabel: How To: Cable Face Pull · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Band pull-apart
alternative.steps: 1. Hold a light resistance band at shoulder height with arms straight. 2. Pull the band apart by squeezing shoulder blades together. 3. Return slowly with control. 4. Keep a slight soft bend at the elbows.

tricepdip.name: Bench dip
how: Place your hands on the edge of a sturdy bench, fingers pointing forward.
Walk feet forward and keep hips close to the bench.
Bend elbows to lower your body in a controlled range.
Push back up without locking the elbows fully.
mistakes: Dipping too deep — strains the shoulder joint.
Letting hips drift too far from the bench.
Shrugging the shoulders up.
tricepdip.cue: Keep your elbows pointed straight back, not flaring out.
tricepdip.videoLabel: How To: Bench Dip · Scott Herman Fitness

alternative.name: Cable triceps pushdown
alternative.steps: 1. Stand at a cable station with a rope or bar attachment. 2. Keep elbows tucked at your sides. 3. Extend your elbows fully, pressing down. 4. Return slowly without moving your upper arms.

barbellrow.name: Barbell bent-over row
how: Stand with feet hip-width apart, grip the barbell just outside your legs.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
Pull the bar toward your lower chest, leading with your elbows.
Lower with control; maintain a flat back throughout.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back.
Jerking the bar with momentum.
Standing too upright — turns it into a shrug.
barbellrow.cue: Brace your core like you're about to take a punch before each rep.
barbellrow.videoLabel: How To: Barbell Bent-Over Row · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Dumbbell bent-over row
alternative.steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width, hinge at hips with flat back, dumbbells hanging. 2. Pull both dumbbells toward your hips simultaneously. 3. Squeeze shoulder blades at the top. 4. Lower slowly and repeat.

splitsquat.name: Bulgarian split squat
how: Stand about two feet in front of a bench and place your rear foot on it.
Hold dumbbells at your sides or keep hands free to start.
Lower your back knee toward the floor in a controlled range.
Drive through your front heel to stand; keep your front knee tracking over your toes.
mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench — causes excessive knee travel.
Torso collapsing forward.
Skipping bodyweight practice before adding load.
splitsquat.cue: Think 'vertical shin on the front leg' as you descend.
splitsquat.videoLabel: How To: Bulgarian Split Squat · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Reverse lunge
alternative.steps: 1. Stand tall and step one foot backward. 2. Bend both knees and lower within a comfortable range. 3. Push through the front foot to return. 4. Alternate sides and use support for balance if needed.

calfmachine.name: Seated calf raise (machine)
how: Sit on the machine with the pad resting on your lower thighs, just above the knees.
Place the balls of your feet on the footplate.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as comfortable.
Lower slowly until you feel a full stretch in the calf.
mistakes: Bouncing through the stretch.
Only doing partial reps at the top.
Using too heavy a load and losing control.
calfmachine.cue: Pause at the top and at the bottom for a full range of motion.
calfmachine.videoLabel: How To: Calf Raises (Science-Based) · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Standing calf raise with support
alternative.steps: 1. Stand beside a wall or sturdy support. 2. Rise onto the balls of both feet. 3. Pause at the top. 4. Lower slowly. Progress to single-leg when stable.

dumbbellshoulder.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
how: Stand tall holding light dumbbells at your sides.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Keep a very slight bend in the elbows throughout.
Lower slowly — this phase builds the muscle.
mistakes: Using too heavy a load and swinging.
Shrugging the shoulders up.
Raising arms above shoulder height.
dumbbellshoulder.cue: Lead with your elbows, not your wrists.
dumbbellshoulder.videoLabel: How To: Lateral Raise · Jeff Nippard

alternative.name: Cable lateral raise
alternative.steps: 1. Set a cable to the lowest position and attach a handle. 2. Stand side-on and hold the handle with the far hand. 3. Raise your arm out to shoulder height with a soft elbow. 4. Lower slowly with continuous cable tension.

treadmill.name: Treadmill walk / jog
how: Start at a slow, comfortable pace and warm up for 2–3 minutes.
Increase speed gradually — walk at 5–6 km/h or jog at 7–9 km/h.
Keep an upright posture and relaxed arm swing.
Cool down at a slow pace for the last 2 minutes.
mistakes: Holding the handrails — reduces caloric burn and posture.
Starting too fast and having to stop early.
Looking down at your feet instead of straight ahead.
treadmill.cue: You should be able to hold a short conversation at the right intensity.
treadmill.videoLabel: Treadmill Running Form Guide · Precision Hydration

alternative.name: Outdoor walk / jog
alternative.steps: 1. Choose a flat, safe route. 2. Warm up with a 2-minute slow walk. 3. Walk briskly or jog at a pace you can sustain. 4. Cool down and stretch lightly.
